method: Interval = shoot time / (clip length x frame rate), with the frame count rounded to the nearest whole frame. The finished clip is frames / frame rate, so it can differ from the target by up to half a frame. Playback speed is shoot time / clip time, which equals interval x frame rate. The whole-second table uses floor(shoot time / interval) frames, matching the fixed-step intervalometers most cameras provide. Assumes a fixed camera position, a constant interval and playback at the chosen frame rate; exposure must stay shorter than the interval, and no motion ramping, flicker correction, stabilisation or file-size estimate is included.
